messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways, 55–75 mph (depending on road type).
• In school zones, 25 mph during school hours. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must be in a child safety seat. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for adults.
• Zero tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for all directions when the bus has its stop sign extended and lights flashing. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking in front of driveways or on sidewalks. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light means stop; green means go (unless a sign indicates otherwise). | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display valid registration and proof of insurance. | | **Towing & Vehicle Inspection** | • Vehicles must pass inspection if required (e.g., commercial). | For detailed statutes, consult the Texas Transportation Code or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles website.
message.reasoning: The user wants information about traffic laws in Texas. We can provide general info. But we might also use the lawsuit_search function? The user didn't ask about lawsuits. They just want traffic laws. So no function call needed. Provide overview.
